head: 5e13888b96d5ab8c25c9db46c64d272bd8ce5d74
claim: a host can add a second account of one provider without any sign-in being moved or overwritten, and is told plainly when a login duplicates an account or re-sign-in is the wrong one

steps.start: a fresh kit on the fake gateway with no account
steps: sign in two different logins in place
sign in as the first login again
start a second sign-in while one runs
sign in again on the first account as another login
read an account context and an unknown one
steps.result: two accounts on their own stores; the repeat answers duplicate, the overlap busy, the wrong re-sign-in identity_mismatch; nothing was moved

verdicts.seen: Read the run summary once: it reports two sign-ins becoming two managed accounts, a duplicate answer with the existing id, a busy answer for overlapping sign-ins, and identity_mismatch with the other account untouched. It also reports exit 0 and that no credential was adopted or copied. This matches the outcome. The gaps it lists (cancel, restart) are not named by the outcome.

Read all 11 entries. Two sign-ins produced openai.ffe0fe and openai.e6bc00, both 'ready' and 'managed'. A repeat sign-in returned why 'duplicate' with existing 'openai.ffe0fe'. Overlapping sign-ins returned 'busy' for one and 'duplicate' for the other. Re-auth as the wrong login returned 'identity_mismatch' with a plain error message. The output ends with 'IN-PLACE OK' and EXIT=0.
